output.summary: Valproate inhibits carnitine-dependent mitochondrial fatty acid transport, leading to hyperammonemia. L-carnitine supplementation (IV 100 mg/kg/day if symptomatic or ammonia >100 µmol/L) reduces valproate-associated hyperammonemia. Abrupt valproate discontinuation carries seizure risk; hyperammonemia is generally manageable with L-carnitine while continuing valproate. Serial ammonia monitoring is recommended.

patient.history_present_illness: Ms. Davis is a 45-year-old African American woman with generalized epilepsy on valproate and SLE on hydroxychloroquine who is brought by ambulance after her husband found her in the bedroom having a continuous generalized seizure lasting at least 25 minutes. She had taken her morning medications but her husband is not sure about her evening valproate from last night. She has been having an SLE flare over the past 2 weeks with significant joint pain, fatigue, and increased corticosteroid need. Her rheumatologist had started her on prednisone 40 mg daily 10 days ago for the SLE flare. She has had two breakthrough seizures in the past year but no prior SE. Her husband noted she was febrile yesterday with temperature 38.2°C. She has lupus nephritis (class III) with mild proteinuria - baseline creatinine 1.1. She has a documented carbamazepine allergy (severe rash, likely SJS).
